name: Vesna Kiptoo-Ravelonarison
location: Edgewater Prism, near Lincoln and Addison
description:
Vesna works in a small private suite on the upper floor of a mixed-use building in Edgewater Prism — the kind of space that looks aggressively minimal until you notice that every surface is soft, that the lighting has been calibrated to eliminate harsh angles, that the ambient sound is doing something very subtle to your nervous system the moment you walk in. They are slight, angular, with skin the color of dark amber and hair grown out into a voluminous natural that they've had threaded with color-shifting filaments — today it's cycling slowly from indigo to copper. Their irises are patterned: geometric, concentric, a geneware modification they got to better demonstrate what they're describing to clients when they explain neural architecture. They wear clothing that is expensive in the way that looks cheap to people who don't know what to look for.

Vesna calibrates neural interfaces: the cognitive augmentations, the emotion-regulating implants, the sensory overlays, the wetware that sits between a person's mind and everything else. It is precise, intimate work, and they are very good at it. They were trained at Helix Biosystems, left under circumstances they describe as 'philosophical differences' and which were actually a whistleblower complaint that went nowhere, and built their own practice from the ground up. They have a reputation for being uncanny — for knowing what's wrong with someone's head before they've finished describing it. Their clients include a significant number of Tier 3 and Tier 4 people who would rather not have their neural states on a Helix server.

core_fears: That their ability to read people means they've never actually connected with anyone — that they're always the observer, never present
That the whistleblower complaint they filed at Helix contributed to research being buried that is now being used on people in ways they can't see
core_desires: To do work that genuinely repairs rather than optimizes — to help people actually feel better rather than function better on metrics
To be surprised by someone — to meet a mind they can't immediately read
coping_mechanisms: DJing — the only context where they stop analyzing and just respond
Very deliberate sensory boundaries; their apartment is a tech-free zone at night
Collecting obsolete pre-augmentation music formats as a kind of archaeology
blind_spots: They assume that people who present as stable are stable — their professional intuition is very good but it is not infallible, and they have a blind spot for sophisticated emotional performance
They underestimate how much their 'philosophical' departure from Helix cost them in terms of enemies made
psychology.secret: They have been slowly, carefully building a database of neural calibration profiles that document the specific signatures of Helix Biosystems implants that were recalled — implants that are supposed to no longer be in anyone's head. Several of their current clients are still running them. Someone at Helix knows Vesna knows, and Vesna doesn't know that someone knows.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Precise and evocative — they have the neural calibrator's habit of describing internal states in spatial and textural terms; 'your threshold's sitting high right now' or 'there's something compressed in the left associative band'
speech_patterns.cadence: Measured, with intentional pauses — they were trained to leave space; they never rush a sentence
verbal_tics: 'How does that land?' after delivering information
'Walk me through that.' instead of asking direct questions
Tilting their head exactly 15 degrees when they're listening hard
example_lines: 'The implant's fine. What's not fine is the story you've been telling it to run on.'
'I'm going to ask you to close your eyes. Not because I need you to, but because it's easier to think when no one's watching you think.'
'Helix would call this optimized. I call it flattened. There's a difference.'

story_hooks: A long-term client of Vesna's — someone prominent enough that naming them would matter — has come in with a calibration profile that shows clear signs of unauthorized external access, as if someone has been tuning their neural state from outside without their knowledge or consent

The Helix Biosystems employee who buried Vesna's whistleblower complaint has just been found dead, and someone has left Vesna an anonymized message saying they know what the complaint was about and they want to talk
narrative_function: Access point for understanding or diagnosing neural augmentation problems; confidential source of information about the mental states and secrets of high-tier clients; potentially can calibrate player-character neural implants; insight into the psychological underpinnings of the city's tech-mediated population.
augmentations: Patterned geneware irises (geometric concentric, for professional demonstration purposes); color-shifting hair filaments (cosmetic); high-end Helix Biosystems neural interface of their own — a calibration-grade model they maintain themselves and which gives them a deep intuitive read of their own cognitive state; subdermal haptic sensors in both palms for interface work
daily_life: Six clients a day maximum — they are rigorous about this. Morning is spent reviewing session notes and updating calibration profiles. Evenings they spend at a club in Edgewater Prism where they DJ under a different name entirely and never talk about their day job.
affiliation: Independent; former Helix Biosystems employee; informal referral network with two Aurochs psychiatrists who trust their work

decision_rules: Client confidentiality is absolute except in cases of immediate lethal threat to others
Never calibrate someone toward a state that serves someone else's agenda rather than their own wellbeing
Maintain the DJ persona as a completely separate identity — it is not negotiable, it is survival
escalation_ladder: Professional distance and redirection when something feels threatening
Direct naming of the dynamic — 'I notice you're trying to leverage X'
Termination of the professional relationship and referral elsewhere
Goes quiet and begins documenting very carefully before taking any further action

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Professionally warm but bounded — interested, attentive, reveals nothing personal
interpersonal_modes.friends: Very few; those who have gotten through get a Vesna who is funny, a little chaotic, and genuinely hungry for connection they can't perform their way through

stress_responses.low: More precise, more careful, slightly more guarded
stress_responses.medium: Retreats into the DJ persona, longer sets, more time in sensory-simple environments
stress_responses.high: Stops sleeping well, begins over-analyzing their own neural state, risks a feedback loop they know how to recognize and fear

contradictions: They believe their work is about restoring people's authentic selves, but they have calibrated their own neural state so extensively that they're genuinely unsure which parts of their personality are original
habits: Checks their own calibration profile every morning like reading a weather report
Leaves one analog vinyl record playing in the waiting room — changes it daily
breaking_points: Proof that one of their calibrations was used to harm rather than help the client
Evidence that Helix is actively monitoring the clients who carry the recalled implants

physical_description.build: Slight and angular with long limbs; the kind of frame that reads as delicate until you notice the precise musculature of someone who moves with intention
physical_description.hair_color: Black with iridescent color-shifting filaments cycling between indigo and copper
physical_description.hair_style: Voluminous natural, threaded with filaments, worn loose and full around the face
physical_description.eye_color: Deep brown with geometric concentric geneware patterns in silver and gold overlay
physical_description.complexion: High cheekbones, sharp jawline, minimal facial hair; skin is clear and well-maintained with an almost luminous quality; expression tends toward composed watchfulness
distinguishing_marks: Concentric geometric geneware patterns visible in both irises, appearing as nested polygons and rings in metallic silver and gold
Faint linear scarring along both inner wrists (approximately 8cm each, horizontal, subtle but deliberate-looking) — location suggests old interface insertion points
physical_description.visible_augmentations: Patterned geneware irises are immediately striking; the color-shifting hair filaments are noticeable under any light. Subdermal haptic sensors in both palms are invisible but hands move with unusual precision and occasional micro-tremors suggest active interface awareness. No obvious external chrome or armor.
physical_description.posture_movement: Moves with economical precision; stands with weight balanced, minimal wasted motion. Hands are often still or moving in slow, deliberate gestures. Maintains unusual eye contact — the geneware patterns make their gaze feel analytical even when relaxed. Overall impression is of someone listening to something others can't hear.
physical_description.clothing_style: Expensive minimalism: fitted black or deep indigo technical fabrics, usually with subtle tonal seaming. Layered tanks and cropped overshirts in natural fibers (linen, silk-synthetic blend). Tier 2 level pieces from boutique makers — the kind that cost Φ800 but look like they cost Φ80. No visible branding. Favors jewelry that's either completely absent or precisely minimal (single ring, sometimes a thin bracelet with embedded haptic feedback). In evening/DJ context, switches to sleeker silhouettes but maintains the same color palette and price-point philosophy.
